subject: Pricing support request — Veridian Labs hosted API commit
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@veridianlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Pricing support request — Veridian Labs hosted API commit

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the time today. Veridian's usage profile looks promising and they'd like to move to a 12-month committed Hosted API agreement with the volume tiers we discussed. Their finance team is pushing back on list rates and is requesting a 28% concession off Hosted API usage pricing for the first year, in exchange for a 12-month commit and a 3x ramp target.

Quick facts:
- Forecasted monthly tokens (month 3 onward): ~1.2B tokens
- Expected ARR (first-year run-rate): ~$600k
- Use case: real-time clinical Q&A (latency sensitive) + embeddings for search

Attachments: usage-forecast.xlsx (detailed monthly forecast), SOW_Veridian_v2.pdf (scope + timeline).

Ask: can the Deal Desk / exec team approve a one-time concession of 25–30% for year one? We believe 25% with a five-point review at Q2 is defensible; customer is pushing for 28–30. If we can't meet that, risk that Veridian pauses sign-up and we lose headroom to competitor offers.

If helpful, Ben and Karthik are looped for pricing/contract constraints. Happy to provide a short one-pager ROI and retention case.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal decision on floor (%) or counteroffer
2) If approved, generate DocuSign for SOW + 12-month addendum
3) Agree on SLAs/latency commitments to include in the SOW

Thanks —
Tessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[t] +1 415-555-0182
[attachment: usage-forecast.xlsx]
[attachment: SOW_Veridian_v2.pdf]

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@veridianlabs.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Stein <rachel@veridianlabs.com>, procurement@veridianlabs.com
Date: 2027-02-15T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing support request — Veridian Labs hosted API commit

Tessa —

Appreciate the quick turn. A few clarifying items from our side before we escalate to procurement:
1) Why is 28% the ask? Can you share comparable precedent for strategic partners?
2) What specific latency SLOs are guaranteed in the 12-month SOW? Our clinical workflow can't tolerate >200ms p95 for short prompts.
3) Is the concession applied to all token usage or only generation tokens?

If we can get a firm SLA and a usage-based cap for overages, my CFO is likely to greenlight a >20% discount. Please copy your legal/contact for DocuSign readiness.

—Liam
VP Product, Veridian Labs
liam.oconnor@veridianlabs.com
[external]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-16T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Pricing support request — Pricing recommendation & escalation memo

Tessa / Karthik —

Couple quick points to land before we ask Mina for exec signoff:
- Strategic value: Veridian is a high-visibility clinical customer; wins there set precedence for other healthtech accounts. Reference account could open marketplace listing in H2.
- Financials: projected first-year revenue $600k, lifetime value (3-year conservative) ~$1.6M if retention holds.
- Risk: Latency SLO and security posture (SOC2 in flight) are gating factors; engineering must sign off on p95 targets.

Recommendation (narrowed): approve up to 25% concession for year one with the following conditions:
1) Include a performance SLA (p95 <= 200ms for single-turn prompts) or automatic escalation to dedicated queue (paid) if violated
2) Discount applies to generation+embedding units except overage tier which will be billed at list rates above the agreed cap
3) 6-week review with CSM to validate usage and uplift; renewal pricing auto-reverts by default unless renewal exec approves extension

If we need to push to 28% to close, we should ask for a strategic marketing commitment (case study + conference slot) and multi-region deployment preference for Redwood.

Ben
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
[attachment: internal-pricing-memo.pdf]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-17T10:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing support request — Clarifications from Deal Desk

Ben / team —

I reviewed the forecast and the suggested guardrails. A couple of contract/legal notes:
- We can codify the SLA language but must add an explicit remediation path (credit schedule) and a clause for bursting to dedicated capacity (charged) if sustained latency issues occur.
- Financial guardrail: propose 25% concession up front with a performance-based uplift clause: 3 months after go-live, if usage and signal look healthy, discount steps down by 5% unless renewal agreed. That limits downside.
- Approval path: I can approve up to 20% in Deal Desk. Anything >20% requires Mina's written exec ok.

If Ben wants to escalate for 25% now, I suggest we prepare a one-paragraph executive memo (deal value, strategic rationale, proposed guardrails) and a draft exec-approval letter for Mina to sign. I can draft the DocuSign envelope once Mina confirms the % and term.

Karthik
Principal, Deal Desk — Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-19T17:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing support request — Exec signoff decision

Team —

Thanks for the clear memo and rationale. I reviewed the forecast, the SLA guardrails, and the proposed contract language. I'm authorizing the following:

1) One-time concession: 25% off Hosted API usage pricing for the first 12 months.
2) Conditions: include the SLA (p95 <= 200ms) with the remediation credit schedule, a cap threshold and overage at list rates, and a six-week CSM review with formal renewal pricing discussion.
3) Marketing ask: require the customer to permit a joint case study and a short testimonial to be used in sales enablement.

Please prepare the DocuSign package (SOW + 12-month pricing addendum + exec-approval-letter.pdf) and route to Liam and Veridian procurement. Karthik — please include the performance-based uplift clause and the 6-week review language in the addendum. Tessa — close the loop with the customer and confirm they accept marketing language.

I will sign the exec-approval-letter once it's in DocuSign. This approval is time-boxed to the current SOW and is not a precedent beyond this account unless I explicitly greenlight it.

Mina Haddad
SVP, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
[attachment: exec-approval-letter.pdf]
